newsitem.title: FINLAND: Bank of Finland seen selling markka - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Finland seen selling markka - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Finland was believed to have intervened in the foreign exchange market in early trade on Monday selling markka for German marks, forex dealers said.
A Bank of Finland official declined comment in line with standard central bank policy.
"Yes, it is clear that they have been there," a forex dealer said. Market operators declined to give any information about the level or amounts of the central bank's intervention.

At 1025/0825, the markka traded at 2.9765 per mark having touched 2.9745. Earlier, dealers said DEM/FIM had broken through support at 2.9750 in Singapore, and that the next support level would be at 2.95 markka againstthe mark.

The markka started to firm strongly late last week after trading briefly above 3.00 per mark early in the week. The Bank of Finland was understood to have intervened last Friday to halt the strengthening by selling markka against the mark.
In October, the markka was linked to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) at a central parity rate of 3.04 per mark.
At 3.00 percent, the Bank of Finland's key monetary policy tool, the tender rate, is on par with the key German repo rate.

The advance of the markka has been fuelled by healthy macro-economic fundamentals -- primarily strong growth expected to outperform most of the rest of Europe, and a wide current account surplus despite a slump in key forest industry exports, analysts say.
